**Finding submitted: deviation (T4C — Termination for convenience).**

- **What's already good:** § 3.4 gives Bluefly a convenience right on one month's notice (effectively the preferred 30 days), and IBM has *no* convenience right anywhere — § 3.3 is breach-only, with IBM expressly barred from collecting early termination charges when it is the breaching party. § 3.4 also keeps IBM performing through the final termination date.
- **Why it still fails the fallback:** § 3.4(b) conditions our exit on "early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A" — uncapped and defined outside the reviewed terms — and § 3.5 makes all accrued amounts due with no refund of prepaid Charges. The playbook fallback tolerates an early-termination fee only up to three months' fees; an uncapped penalty can make the convenience right illusory.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** cap the Attachment A charges at three (3) months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services, and add a 30-day refund of Charges prepaid for periods after the termination date.
